messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — [SEV2] euc2 AZ-b ingress cluster: sustained 5xx spike across ALB -> envoy frontends (>=30% 5xx over 3m). auto-escalation to oncall.

oncall_maria: on it. seeing alerts and high error rate on euc2-ingress-alb-b. pulling logs now.

sre_alex: pinged. any customer-facing impact yet?

oncall_maria: synthetic checks failing with 502/504, internal healthchecks flapping. TL;DR: ~30% of euc2 traffic hitting AZ-b shows connreset/502 from envoy. AZ-a mostly OK.

eng_jordan: copying perf dashboard — upstream target group errors and Envoy downstream conn resets. likely backend keepalive/connection churn or NLB health probe flapping.

net_kim: checking NLB target health. I see targetgroup tg-euc2-b has many Targets Unhealthy, health reason: connection reset (RST) from instances.

oncall_maria: running quick curl smoke against the ingress LB in AZ-b:
```
curl -sS -I https://ingress-euc2-b.example.net/health || true
```
returns 502/504 intermittently.

deploy-bot: deploy event: ingress-controller/1.12.4 rolled in euc2 AZ-b ~ 30m ago by eng_jordan. no automatic rollbacks.

eng_jordan: confirm I pushed a config tweak (keepalive timeout adjust) ~32m ago. investigating correlation.

net_kim: routing-wise nothing in route53 changed. no DNS drift. but I do see increased TCP resets at AZ-b network interface around the same time. Could be noisy neighbor or underlying host NIC flapping.

pm_troy: any customer escalations yet? we should be ready to notify if impact is >10% region traffic or enterprise customers affected.

oncall_maria: quick impact estimate from edge metrics: ~22% of euc2 requests are 5xx (peaked 38%). Global traffic: euc2 is ~18% of total, so estimate ~4% global error. Two enterprise tenants show elevated error rates (IDs redacted).

sre_alex: ok. immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce weight for euc2 AZ-b in weighted DNS/traffic splitter to 0 for ~5m 2) drain targets in tg-euc2-b 3) trigger ingress controller restart only if draining doesn't normalize.

oncall_maria: starting traffic shift. applying traffic-split change now:
```
# infra-cli traffic-split set euc2:azb=0 euc2:aza=1 --dry-run=false
```

oncall_maria: traffic-split applied. watching error rate.

(2m later)
oncall_maria: errors dropping in AZ-b from 38% -> 6% within 2m after weight change. global 5xx down to ~1.2%. looks promising.

net_kim: starting drain on tg-euc2-b targets to avoid immediate reconnections:
```
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn tg-euc2-b --targets "[]" # drain
```

eng_jordan: curious if the controller change caused a regression with older Envoy keepalive behavior. saving logs from the controller pods.

oncall_maria: marking customer impact: partial degraded access for customers routed to euc2 AZ-b for ~25 minutes before mitigation. notified trust-ASAP?

pm_troy: yes please draft a short blurb for status page: impacted region euc2, partial errors, mitigation in progress, some customers may have seen intermittent 502/504. I'll review.

deploy-bot: monitor: ingress-controller pods in euc2 AZ-b show repeated LivenessProbe restarts over 40m (count 6).

sre_alex: given drain succeeded, keep weight change for now. next: replace EC2 instances in AZ-b host pool (suspected NIC faults) and coordinate with infra to reprovision. net_kim, can you kick off host rotation?

net_kim: opening host-rotation job for euc2 AZ-b. replacing 3 hosts in the pool one-at-a-time to avoid capacity loss. ETA ~25m.

eng_jordan: I'm preparing a rollback of the keepalive change to test if it stops liveness restarts — but only after host rotation if errors reoccur. will not push blindly.

oncall_maria: updating status channel and incident timeline. posting to #customer-status: "We experienced partial 5xx errors in euc2 affecting some customers. We shifted traffic and drained unhealthy targets; traffic has normalized. We're replacing hosts in AZ-b and investigating root cause."

pm_troy: thanks. please include estimated window and that some enterprise customers were impacted; ops will follow up for post-incident RCA.

(15m later)

oncall_maria: host rotation started. ingress errors remain low (<1% 5xx). healthchecks stable.

net_kim: replaced host host-azb-03; monitoring NIC metrics. no obvious hardware error logs yet. continuing rotation.

deploy-bot: automatic pager suppression engaged after error rate stayed below threshold for 10m.

sre_alex: good. handoff plan: I'll take on-call for remainder of incident and do the post-mortem. oncall_maria, can you write short timeline and commands you ran?

oncall_maria: making timeline notes now. key commands: traffic-split set, aws elbv2 drain, curl checks, checked controller pod logs (`kubectl logs -n ingress ... --since=1h`).

eng_jordan: saved controller logs and container metrics to /var/tmp/incident-1779991111.tar.gz and uploaded to S3. will attach to postmortem.

pm_troy: customer comms queued. I'll notify the two affected enterprise accounts directly with root-cause follow-up when we have RCA.

sre_alex: next steps for RCA: collect NIC metrics, instance serial console logs, pod restarts, config diff for ingress controller (compare pre/post keepalive). schedule 1hr RCA meeting tomorrow. assign to eng_jordan + net_kim + oncall_maria.

oncall_maria: handoff: incident in mitigation state, traffic shifted away from AZ-b, host rotation in progress (1/3 done), global error rate normal. handing to @sre_alex for investigation + postmortem.

sre_alex: taking it. thanks @oncall_maria. I'll update this thread with postmortem link and timeline when ready. :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigating -> monitoring. severity downgraded to SEV3.

pm_troy: closing customer-facing note after I get verbals from eng. thanks team.

(End of thread)
